description: This course, offered by the Department of Humanities & Social Sciences, is designed to introduce the concepts of business to students and aims to acquaint them with business processes from beginning to the end.

syllabus.title: Fundamentals of Business
syllabus.body: Business: Meaning and Characteristics of Business, Objectives of Business. Classification of Business Activities: Industry and Commerce, Industry types: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary. Types of Businesses: Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Limited Liability Company, Private and Public company. Formation of Company: stages and required documents.

syllabus.title: Sources of Business Finance
syllabus.body: Business Finance: Concept and Importance. Types of Sources of Finance: Long-term Sources (Equity Shares, Preference shares, Debentures, Term Loans, Retained earnings, Loan from financial institutions, etc.), Short Term Sources (Trade Credit, Accrued Expenses, Commercial Papers, Public Deposits etc.)

syllabus.title: Small Business and Entrepreneurship Development
syllabus.body: Entrepreneurship Development (ED): Concept, Characteristics and Need. Process of Entrepreneurship Development: Start-up India Scheme, Intellectual Property Rights and Entrepreneurship. Small Scale Enterprise: Classification and Roles; Issues and Challenges faced by Small Scale Enterprises, Government schemes for small scale industries.

syllabus.title: Business Services and Social Responsibility of Businesses
syllabus.body: Business services: Meaning and Types, Emerging Modes of Business, E-business: Concept, Scope and Benefits, E-commerce, EDI, Web-based Marketing, Role of Internet and Risk Management; Social Responsibility of Business. Role of Business in Sustainable Development.

outcomes: Understand different forms and numerous processes of a business.
Practice the ethical behaviour of businesses.
textbooks: Business Studies: Learners Book, Oxford Successful
Business Studies: 2018/19 Undergraduate Guide, University of Huddersfield
Business Studies, Fourth Edition, Ian Chambers and David Gray, CP.
